p.src: Now it happened that the constables seized Tang Niu'er and escorted him into the county yamen. When the magistrate heard that a murder had been committed, he hurried out and took his seat in the court. The constables crowded around Tang Niu'er and brought him before the court. The magistrate looked and saw an old woman kneeling on the left and a man kneeling on the right. The magistrate asked, “What is this murder case?” The old woman stated, “My surname is Yan. I had a daughter called Poxi, whom I gave to Clerk Song as his kept woman. Last night my daughter was drinking with Song Jiang when this Tang Niu'er came expressly to make trouble, shouting abuse as he went out; all the neighbors know of it. This morning Song Jiang went out for a while, then returned and killed my daughter. I grappled with him and dragged him before the county office, but this Tang the Second beat me off and snatched Song Jiang away. I beg Your Honor to see justice done.” The magistrate said, “How dare you rogue beat her off and rescue the murderer?” Tang Niu'er pleaded, “This humble man knew nothing of what had happened. Last night I merely went to find Song Jiang and cadge a bowl of wine, but Granny Yan drove me out. This morning I went out to sell pickled ginger and happened upon Granny Yan grappling with Clerk Song before the county office. When I saw them, I wrongly stepped in to make peace, and he then went away. But I had no idea that he had killed her daughter.” The magistrate shouted, “Nonsense! Song Jiang is an honorable and honest man. How could he rashly commit murder? This death must surely be your doing. Where are the attendants?” He immediately summoned the clerks on duty in the court.

p.src: Presently Clerk Zhang Wenyuan came forward. When he heard that Granny Yan accused Song Jiang of murdering her daughter, he knew this was the very woman with whom he was having an affair. He at once took down everyone's testimony, wrote out Granny Yan's complaint for her, and compiled the case file. They summoned the local coroner and his assistants, together with the ward officers, village headman, neighbors, and all others concerned. They went to Granny Yan's house, opened the door, brought out the corpse, and formally examined it. Beside the body lay the knife used in the crime. After repeated examination that day, they determined that she had been killed while alive by a knife drawn across her throat. When the inquest was duly completed, they placed the corpse in a coffin and deposited it at a temple, then took all concerned back to the county office.

p.src: The constables took the official document and went to Squire Song's manor in Song Family Village. The old squire came out to receive them and, when they had reached the rustic hall, seated them. The constables produced the writ and handed it to the old squire to read. Squire Song said, “Honored officers, please be seated and allow this old man to explain. My family has farmed for generations, and we have lived by tending these fields and gardens. My unfilial son Song Jiang was disobedient from childhood. Refusing to earn an honest living, he insisted on becoming a clerk, and no amount of remonstrance would sway him. Therefore, several years ago, I reported his disobedience to the officials of this county and had him struck from my family register, so he is no longer counted as a member of my household. He lived on his own in the county town, while I remained here in this remote village with my son Song Qing, living from our few acres of land. He and I share neither water nor grain and have no dealings with one another. I feared that he might cause trouble and bring calamity upon us, so I made that report under the former magistrate and obtained a certificate, which I have kept here as proof. I shall fetch it and show it to you gentlemen.” All the constables were friendly with Song Jiang. They knew perfectly well that this was an escape route prepared in advance, but nothing could induce them to make an enemy of him. They replied, “Since you have the certificate, Squire, bring it for us to see. We shall copy it and report back to the county office.” The old squire immediately had chickens and geese slaughtered, set out wine to entertain them, presented them with more than ten taels of silver, and produced the official certificate for them to copy. The constables took leave of Squire Song and returned to report to the magistrate, saying, “Squire Song had Song Jiang struck from the register three years ago and obtained an official certificate. Here is a copy of it. We cannot summon or arrest him.” Since the magistrate likewise wished to exonerate Song Jiang, he said, “As there is an official certificate and he has no other relatives, we need only offer a reward of one thousand strings of cash, send notices everywhere, and have him hunted down and arrested.”

p.src: Zhang the Third again incited Granny Yan to go before the court. With her hair loose and disheveled, she cried, “Song Jiang is in fact being hidden at home by Song Qing, who will not let him surrender to the authorities. Why will Your Honor not see justice done for this old woman and have Song Jiang arrested?” The magistrate shouted, “His father reported his disobedience to the authorities three years ago and had him struck from the register. An official certificate remains as proof. How can I seize his father and brother and force them to produce him?” Granny Yan pleaded, “Your Honor, who does not know that he is called the Filial and Righteous Black Third Son? That certificate is false. I beg Your Honor to see justice done!” The magistrate said, “Nonsense! How can an official document sealed under the former magistrate be false?” Below the court, Granny Yan cried out against the injustice and her bitter plight. Choking with sobs, she appealed to the magistrate: “A human life is weightier than heaven. If you refuse to see justice done for this old woman, I shall have no choice but to lodge my complaint at the prefectural office. My poor daughter died so cruel a death!” Zhang the Third again came before the court and spoke on her behalf: “If Your Honor does not issue orders to arrest the man and this Granny Yan appeals to the higher authorities, the consequences will be serious. If an inquiry should come down, this humble clerk will find it difficult to answer.” The magistrate knew there was reason in this and had no choice but to seal an official writ. He then commissioned the two chief constables, Zhu Tong and Lei Heng, before the court: “Take a large party of men to Squire Song's manor in Song Family Village and search for and arrest the offender Song Jiang.” A poem bears witness: When a matter touches not the heart, one lets it run its course; yet who upon the road resents a flower being plucked? But grieving that flower-like Poxi had died, a handsome lover became a bitter foe.

p.src: Chief constables Zhu and Lei received the official warrant, mustered more than forty local soldiers, and headed straight for the Song family manor. When Old Master Song learned of their arrival, he hurried out to meet them. Zhu Tong and Lei Heng said, “Please do not blame us, Old Master. We have been sent by our superiors and have no choice in the matter. Where is your son, Clerk Song, now?” Old Master Song replied, “Honored chief constables, that unfilial son of mine, Song Jiang, has nothing whatever to do with this old man. Under the former magistrate, I formally had him removed from my household, and the certificate issued upon my petition is here. For over three years Song Jiang and I have been registered as separate households. He has not lived with my family, nor has he ever returned to the manor.” Zhu Tong said, “Even so, we must invite guests by written card and summon men by official warrant. We cannot simply take your word that he is not at the manor. Allow us to search the place so that we may return with an answer.” He then ordered thirty or forty local soldiers to surround the manor. “I shall guard the front gate myself. Chief Constable Lei, you go in and search first.” Lei Heng entered and searched the front and rear of the manor. Coming out, he told Zhu Tong, “He truly is not here.” Zhu Tong said, “I still cannot set my mind at ease. Chief Constable Lei, guard the gate with our brothers while I make a thorough search myself.” Old Master Song said, “I am a man who knows the law. How would I dare conceal him in my manor?” Zhu Tong replied, “This is a murder case, so you cannot blame us.” The old master said, “Do as you please, Chief Constable. Go and search as carefully as you wish.” Zhu Tong said, “Chief Constable Lei, keep watch over the old master here. Do not let him move about.”

p.src: Zhu Tong entered the manor alone, leaned his cudgel-blade against the wall, and bolted the door. He went into the Buddhist hall, dragged the altar table aside, and lifted a section of the floorboards. Beneath the boards lay the end of a cord. He gave it a single pull; a bronze bell rang, and Song Jiang crawled out of the underground chamber. The sight of Zhu Tong gave him a great fright. Zhu Tong said, “Brother Gongming, do not blame your younger brother for coming to arrest you today. You and I have always been the closest of friends, and we have kept nothing from one another. One day over wine, you told me, ‘Beneath the Buddha pedestal in my house is an underground chamber. The Buddhas of the Three Ages stand above it, and a floorboard in the Buddhist hall covers it, with an altar table set on top. If ever you find yourself in grave danger, you may come and hide here.’ I heard you then and kept it in mind. Today, when the magistrate of our county sent Lei Heng and me here, I had no choice but to keep up appearances before outsiders. His Honor also wishes to spare you, but Zhang San and that woman spoke out in the hall, declaring that if the county did not see justice done, they would surely lodge a complaint with the prefecture. That is why he sent the two of us to search your manor again. I feared Lei Heng might insist on doing everything by the book and prove unable to protect anyone; if he should see you, there would be no way to smooth things over. So I contrived to leave him at the front of the manor and came straight here to speak with you myself. This place may be well concealed, but it is no safe refuge. If anyone learns of it and searches here, what will you do?” Song Jiang said, “I have been thinking the same thing myself. Had you not protected me so carefully, worthy brother, I would surely have suffered the calamity of chains and imprisonment.” Zhu Tong said, “Please do not speak so. Where do you intend to seek refuge?” Song Jiang said, “I have considered three places where I might find refuge: first, the manor of ‘Little Whirlwind’ Chai Jin in Henghai Commandery, Cangzhou; second, the home of ‘Little Li Guang’ Hua Rong at Qingfeng Stockade in Qingzhou; and third, the manor of Old Master Kong on White Tiger Mountain. He has two sons: the elder is called ‘Comet’ Kong Ming, and the younger ‘Lone Fire Star’ Kong Liang. They have often come to the county town to meet me. I am still wavering among those three places and cannot decide which one to seek out.” Zhu Tong said, “Brother, you must decide quickly and leave as soon as you have decided. You should set out tonight. By no means delay and bring ruin upon yourself.” Song Jiang said, “I rely entirely upon you, brother, to manage matters with the authorities high and low. Whenever money is needed, come and take it without hesitation.” Zhu Tong said, “Set your mind at ease. I shall take care of all that. You need only make arrangements for your journey.” Song Jiang thanked Zhu Tong and went back into the underground chamber.

p.src: Zhu Tong and Lei Heng called the local soldiers together, and they all entered the thatched hall. Old Master Song hurriedly ordered wine to be served to entertain them. Zhu Tong said, “Do not trouble to prepare food and wine. For now, would the old master and Fourth Son please accompany us to the county office?” Lei Heng asked, “Why is Fourth Son nowhere to be seen?” Old Master Song said, “I sent him to a nearby village to have some farming implements made, so he is not at the manor. As for that scoundrel Song Jiang, three years ago I had the unfilial wretch struck from my household. I still have the official certificate here as proof.” Zhu Tong said, “That excuse will never pass! The two of us act under the magistrate’s express command to arrest you and your son. Come to the county office and answer for yourselves.” Lei Heng said, “Chief Constable Zhu, hear me out. There must have been some cause behind Clerk Song’s crime, and it may not yet be an offense deserving death. Since the old master already has a certificate bearing an official seal, and it is no forgery, let us for the sake of our former friendship with Clerk Song shoulder a little responsibility for him. We need only copy the certificate and take it back to report.” Zhu Tong thought, “I deliberately said the opposite so that he would not suspect me.” Zhu Tong said, “Since you put it that way, brother, there is no reason for me to play the villain.” Old Master Song thanked them, saying, “I am deeply grateful for the consideration shown by both chief constables.” He at once had food and wine set out to reward the company. Then he brought out twenty taels of silver and presented them to the two chief constables. Zhu Tong and Lei Heng firmly refused it and instead distributed the money among the forty local soldiers. After making a copy of the official certificate, they bade farewell to Old Master Song and departed from Song Family Village. The two chief constables, Zhu and Lei, then led the whole company back to the county town.

p.src: Now, Song Jiang came from a farming household, so how did his family possess such an underground vault? The reason was that under the Song dynasty it was easy to be an official but exceedingly difficult to be a clerk. Why was it easy to be an official? Because treacherous ministers then held sway at court and slanderous flatterers monopolized power: they appointed none but their own associates and accepted none who brought no money. And why was it exceedingly difficult to be a clerk? In those days, if a court clerk committed an offense, the lighter punishment was tattooing and exile to some distant and pestilential military prefecture; the heavier meant confiscation of the family property and an end to his miserable life. For that reason, such men prepared places like this beforehand in which to hide. Fearing that their parents might also be implicated, they had them lodge a charge of unfilial conduct, strike their names from the household register, and establish separate households. The authorities would issue documents certifying that they had no dealings with one another, though the family property remained in the same house. Many people in the Song dynasty made such arrangements.

p.src: That evening the two brothers tied up their bundles. They rose during the fourth watch, washed, ate an early meal, dressed for travel, and set out. Song Jiang wore a white Fanyang felt hat and a white satin tunic, fastened with a plum-red cord of lengthwise weave; his lower legs were wrapped in gaiters, and on his feet were hemp shoes with many loops. Song Qing dressed as an attendant and shouldered the bundle. Together they went before the thatched hall and bowed farewell to their father, Old Master Song. All three shed tears without cease. The old master exhorted them, “A long road and a great future lie before you both; do not give way to sorrow.” Song Jiang and Song Qing then instructed all the servants, high and low, to guard the household carefully, attend diligently on the old master morning and evening, and see that he lacked nothing to eat or drink. Each brother girded on a short saber and took up a long-handled broadsword, then went straight out of Song Family Village.

p.src: When Lord Chai saw Song Jiang, he bowed to the ground and said, “How sorely Chai Jin has longed to see you! By heaven’s grace, what happy wind has blown you here today, fulfilling the longing of my whole life? What great fortune! What great fortune!” Song Jiang also bowed to the ground and replied, “I am but an ignorant, unworthy clerk, and today I have come especially to seek refuge with you.” Chai Jin helped Song Jiang to his feet, saying, “Last night the lampwick blossomed, and this morning magpies called. Little did I think it foretold the arrival of my honored brother.” His face was wreathed in smiles. Song Jiang was delighted by the warmth of Chai Jin’s welcome and called his younger brother Song Qing forward to be introduced. Chai Jin ordered his attendants to take Clerk Song’s luggage to their quarters beneath the western veranda of the rear hall. Taking Song Jiang by the hand, Chai Jin led him into the main inner hall, where host and guest took their appointed seats. Chai Jin said, “May I venture to ask: I heard that you were employed in Yuncheng County. How did you find the leisure to visit my humble country dwelling?” Song Jiang replied, “I have long heard your illustrious name, my lord; it has rung in my ears like thunder. Though I repeatedly received your honored letters, I regretted that my lowly duties left me no leisure to meet you. Today, unworthy Song Jiang has committed a deed from which there is no escape. My brother and I could think of nowhere to shelter, until I remembered your devotion to justice and generosity with wealth, and so we came especially to seek refuge with you.” When Chai Jin had heard him out, he smiled and said, “Set your mind at ease, brother. Even if you had committed all ten abominable crimes, now that you have reached my estate, you need not worry. Chai Jin does not boast idly: whatever constables or government troops may come, they dare not even look my little estate squarely in the eye.” Song Jiang then related in full how he had killed Yan Poxi. Chai Jin burst out laughing and said, “Have no fear, brother. Even if you had killed an imperial official and plundered the treasury of a prefecture, I, Chai Jin, would still dare conceal you on my estate.” Having said this, he invited Song Jiang and his brother to bathe. He immediately brought out two sets of clothes, headcloths, silk shoes, and clean socks, and had the brothers replace the old garments they had worn before bathing. After bathing, both men put on the new clothes. The servants carried the brothers’ old clothes to their sleeping quarters. Chai Jin invited Song Jiang into the innermost rear hall, where food and wine had already been laid out. He seated Song Jiang in the place of honor and took the seat opposite him. As Song Jiang, his elder brother, occupied the higher place, Song Qing sat to one side.

Truly, when his name was spoken, stars and moon lost their radiance; when his identity was revealed, rivers ran backward through the land.
But who was the man whose identity Lord Chai revealed? Listen to the explanation in the next chapter.
